reason: The rough edge can create the skin and vessel break described in the chapter.
expectation: The body will have a small cut that needs to be sealed.

effect: The cut has exposed a bleeding vessel, so platelets are the next likely part of the response.
reaction: The narrowed vessel is a useful detail.
reason: Platelets at the cut should help form an initial plug in the damaged vessel.
expectation: Platelets will gather at the injury and begin to limit bleeding.

effect: The platelet plug slows the leak; clotting factors and fibrinogen may help reinforce it.
reaction: The initial plug is a clear first response to the injury.
reason: Activated clotting factors should act on fibrinogen to form material that strengthens the plug.
expectation: Fibrinogen will be converted into fibrin for the clot.

effect: The clotting factors produced fibrin threads, which can now reinforce the platelet plug.
reaction: The thread mesh makes the reinforcement easy to picture.
reason: The fibrin threads should strengthen the plug at the damaged vessel.
expectation: The fibrin mesh will stabilize the platelet plug and stop the bleeding.

effect: The fibrin mesh stabilized the platelet plug and stopped the bleeding, while the skin remained open.
reaction: The distinction between sealing the vessel and closing the skin was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding fibrin to the platelet plug was most worthwhile because it connected the two parts of the clot and showed how the leak was stopped.

leastWorthwhile.text: Creating the cut was a predictable setup step, though it made the injury clear.

surprise.text: The vessel was sealed while the skin above it remained open; stopping bleeding and repairing the skin are separate events.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary. Each followed the visible injury or the developing clot.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the open skin repairs itself. This chapter made the clotting sequence clear, although its choices were mostly predictable.
